outcome: No source I could read records a resolution of the Erdős–Turán conjecture since 26 January 2024, and every standard reference I opened still lists it as open. The only in-window claim of a full proof is Theophilus Agama’s arXiv:1707.05679, whose text first asserted the full conjecture on 5 January 2024 (before the frozen revision) and kept it in versions of 13 February and 8 March 2024; it has no referee or journal record, its own corollary is restricted and concedes a step, and the same author’s March 2026 arXiv paper still calls the conjecture unresolved. The AI-involved results found (Erdős Problems 868, 870, 871 and an OpenAI short-proofs preprint) concern neighbouring Erdős–Nathanson or splitting questions, not the unboundedness of representation counts.
problem_asks: (a) Hypothesis, as the bullet words it: B is an additive basis of order 2, i.e. every sufficiently large integer is a sum of two elements of B (literature: an asymptotic basis of order 2). (b) Conclusion, as the bullet words it: the number of ways a positive integer n is written as a sum of two elements of B tends to infinity as n tends to infinity, a limit. (c) The literature form (Erdős and Turán 1941; Nathanson’s surveys; Wikipedia’s lead; Agama’s Conjecture 1.1) is limsup of that count = ∞, which is weaker than the bullet’s limit. (d) Points the bullet leaves open: whether pairs are ordered (literature: r(n) = #{(a,b) in B×B : a+b=n}, ordered); the bullet says positive integers n while the literature uses the nonnegative integers. There is one question here, the unboundedness of order-2 representation counts; it has no further parts.

events.what_happened: G. A. Dirac, ‘Note on a problem in additive number theory’, J. London Math. Soc. 26 (1951), 312–313, is listed by the Open Problem Garden entry as showing that the representation function of an asymptotic basis of order 2 cannot be constant from some point on. Partial result, pre-window.
events.delivers: Rules out eventual constancy of r_B(n). Does not show limsup r_B(n) = ∞ or r_B(n) → ∞.
events.remains: Whether limsup r_B(n) = ∞ (the literature form), and whether r_B(n) → ∞ (the bullet’s literal form).

checked_by.who: Journal of the London Mathematical Society
checked_by.what_they_did: published the note (citation only; I did not open the paper)

events.direction: Partial result in the direction of the conjecture (non-constancy), not a resolution of it.

events.what_happened: Per the erdosproblems.com page for Problem 868: Härtter (1956) and Nathanson (1974) proved that there exist additive bases of order 2 containing no minimal additive basis. This is a neighbouring question (minimal subbases), pre-window. Recorded because the erdosproblems page cites it as background to the Erdős–Nathanson family.
events.delivers: Existence of order-2 bases with no minimal subbasis. Concerns minimal subbases, not the growth of r_B(n).
events.doubts: Only the erdosproblems.com citation was read; the original papers were not opened.
events.direction: Neighbouring result; no direction on the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Erdős (1956) showed that an order-2 basis can have representation counts of order log n, close to optimal, which led him to ask whether limsup r(n)/log n > 0 for any basis (as summarised by the Wikipedia article). Erdős and Tetali (1990) extended the existence result to bases of arbitrary order. Pre-window.
events.delivers: Existence of bases with r(n) = O(log n). This is an upper-bound construction. It is compatible with limsup r(n) = ∞, because log n itself tends to infinity. It is not a lower bound and does not settle the conjecture.
events.remains: The conjecture as stated: whether every such basis has unbounded representation counts.
events.doubts: A 2011 Waterloo MSc thesis (see xiao-2011-thesis-claim below) describes this 1956 result as ‘a positive answer’ to the h = 2 conjecture. That reading conflicts with the upper-bound description here. Recorded as a dispute.
events.direction: Upper-bound construction. Does not cut toward or against unboundedness.
events.object: Existence of a basis of order 2 whose representation count is O(log n). Probabilistic (Erdős); later derandomised by Kolountzakis per a 2024 arXiv summary.

events.what_happened: Erdős and Nathanson (1979), as cited on erdosproblems.com for Problem 868: if 1_A*1_A(n) > (log 4/3)^(-1) log n for all large n, then A contains a minimal additive basis of order 2, and A decomposes into two disjoint bases. Pre-window. Neighbouring question (Erdős–Nathanson family), not the Erdős–Turán conjecture.
events.delivers: A logarithmic threshold with constant above (log 4/3)^(-1) forces minimal subbases and decomposability. The hypothesis is a lower bound on r, and divergence of r is assumed in the neighbouring Problem 871.
events.remains: The Erdős–Turán conjecture (which asks whether r must diverge at all).
events.direction: Conditional result in a neighbouring question. Its hypothesis already requires a logarithmic lower bound on r, which is stronger than the conjecture’s conclusion.

events.what_happened: P. Borwein, S. Choi and F. Chu, ‘An old conjecture of Erdős–Turán on additive bases’, Math. Comp. 75 (2006), 475–484 (DOI 10.1090/s0025-5718-05-01777-1; online date 2005 per a catalogue record). They show that the representation count of an order-2 basis cannot be bounded by 7, so limsup r ≥ 8. Pre-window.
events.revisions: Issue year 2006 (vol. 75, no. 253). Online publication year 2005 per catalogue.
events.delivers: Lower bound: limsup r_B(n) ≥ 8 for every order-2 basis (summaries say ‘cannot be bounded by 7’). Does not show limsup = ∞.
events.remains: Whether limsup r_B(n) = ∞, and the bullet’s literal limit form.
events.doubts: Bound value differs across sources: 7 in the Wikipedia summary and the Waterloo thesis; 8 as the new lower bound in later summaries. I did not open the paper.
events.direction: Partial lower bound, consistent with the conjecture’s direction. Not a resolution.

events.what_happened: Erdős and Nathanson (1989), as cited on erdosproblems.com for Problems 868 and 871: for every t there is an order-2 basis with 1_A*1_A(n) ≥ t for all large n that cannot be partitioned into two disjoint bases of order 2. Pre-window. Neighbouring question.
events.delivers: Bases with bounded-below (and arbitrarily large) representation counts that are not decomposable. Shows divergence is not sufficient for decomposability when the bound is a constant t. Concerns a different property from the conjecture.
events.doubts: Only the erdosproblems.com citation was read.
events.direction: Neighbouring result; no direction on the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Grekos, Haddad, Helou and Pihko show that limsup r(n) ≥ 6 for every asymptotic basis of order 2 (as cited in later summaries). Publication cited as ‘Supremum of representation functions’, Integers 11 (2011), A30, and ‘On the general Erdős–Turán conjecture’, Int. J. Combinatorics (2014). Year uncertain: the 2011 date is from a search summary, not an opened paper.
events.revisions: Year uncertain. The lower bound 6 is also reported as 5 in one summary.
events.delivers: Lower bound limsup r ≥ 6. Does not show limsup = ∞.
events.remains: Whether limsup r = ∞, and the bullet’s literal limit form.
events.doubts: The year and the value 6 vs 5 conflict across sources; not resolved.
events.direction: Partial lower bound, consistent with the conjecture’s direction.

events.what_happened: Sándor (2008), ‘A note on a conjecture of Erdős–Turán’, Integers A30, as summarised in a search result: if limsup r(n) = A for a positive integer A, then liminf r(n) ≤ A − 2√A + 1. Pre-window.
events.delivers: A relation between limsup and liminf of r when limsup is finite. It assumes limsup = A, so it does not decide whether limsup = ∞.
events.doubts: Read only from search summaries.
events.direction: Conditional on limsup being finite; no direction on the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Konstantoulas (2013), ‘Lower bounds for a conjecture of Erdős and Turán’, Acta Arith. 159 (per the IMPAN catalogue URL): if the complement of A+A has small upper density (as for asymptotic bases), then infinitely many n have more than five representations. Pre-window. Lower bound only.
events.delivers: Infinitely many n with more than five representations, under small upper density of the complement. A lower bound on limsup-type behaviour, weaker than Borwein–Choi–Chu’s ≥ 8.
events.doubts: Read from a search summary only.
events.direction: Partial lower bound, consistent with the conjecture’s direction.

events.what_happened: Tang and Chen (2008, J. Number Theory per the ScienceDirect URL) construct a basis of order 2 for Z_m with bounded representation counts, so the modular analogue of the conjecture is false. Constant quoted as 768 in one summary and 5120 in another; the exact bound is not resolved. Pre-window; modular, not the integers.
events.delivers: In Z_m, bounded representation counts occur for order-2 bases, for every m. This is a different group from the integers and says nothing about N.
events.doubts: Constant conflicts across summaries (768, 5120). Paper not opened.
events.direction: Counterexample for the modular analogue. Does not cut against the integer conjecture.
events.object: A set A in Z_m with A + A = Z_m and bounded representation counts (bound 768 or 5120 per summaries). Construction not read.

events.what_happened: Ruzsa (1990), as summarised in a search result: a basis A of the nonnegative integers whose representation function is bounded in square mean. This shows that a proof of the conjecture cannot rest on the mean-square behaviour of r alone. Pre-window; not opened.
events.delivers: A basis with bounded mean-square representation count. This is compatible with r being unbounded in the limsup sense, so it does not decide the conjecture.
events.doubts: Read only from a search summary; the citation details are unverified.
events.direction: A barrier-type result; no direction on the conjecture.
events.object: A basis of N with bounded mean-square representation function. Construction not read.

events.what_happened: Stanley Yao Xiao, ‘On the Erdős–Turán conjecture and related results’, MSc thesis, University of Waterloo (issued 2011-08-29). Its abstract states: ‘The case for h = 2 was given a positive answer by Erdös in 1956.’ and ‘The case for arbitrary h was given by Erdös and Tetali in 1990.’ It also says the 1956 and 1990 proofs are probabilistic and non-explicit.
events.delivers: As worded, a claim that the conjecture was given a positive answer for h = 2 in 1956. That reading conflicts with the description of the 1956 result as the existence of economical bases (r = O(log n)), which is an upper bound and does not give unboundedness. I read this as a misstatement of the economical-basis result, but I record it as a claim.
events.remains: On the thesis’s own wording, nothing; on the literature’s description of the 1956 result, the conjecture.
events.doubts: The thesis’s reading of the 1956 result is at odds with the Wikipedia article and with the economical-basis description in later summaries. It is an MSc thesis with no referee record found. Its ‘positive answer’ wording is the only place I found this claim.
events.direction: As worded, a claimed resolution for h = 2 (direction: unbounded). Contradicted by the literature’s description of the 1956 result.

events.what_happened: Vishesh Jain, Huy Tuan Pham, Mehtaab Sawhney and Dmitrii Zakharov, ‘An explicit economical additive basis’, arXiv:2405.08650 (first submitted 14 May 2024), give an explicit subset A of the nonnegative integers with A+A = all of N, such that the number of ordered pairs summing to N grows slower than any positive power of N. The abstract says it ‘answers a question of Erdős’ (which question is not stated in the abstract page I read).
events.revisions: v1 14 May 2024; later versions not checked.
events.delivers: An upper bound on the representation count (N^(o(1)) growth), explicit. Compatible with unbounded counts, since it does not show boundedness. It does not bear on the conjecture’s direction.
events.remains: Whether limsup r = ∞ (the conjecture is a lower-bound statement and this is an upper bound).
events.doubts: Only the abstract page was read, so the precise Erdős question it answers is unknown to me.
events.direction: Upper-bound construction; not a resolution of the conjecture in either direction.
events.object: An explicit set A of nonnegative integers with A+A covering N and r(N) = N^(o(1)). Explicit (not probabilistic), per the abstract as summarised.

events.what_happened: Theophilus Agama, ‘On the Erdős–Turán additive base conjecture’, arXiv:2010.11857 (v1 16 Oct 2020; v2 9 Jun 2021; v3 12 Mar 2026). Abstract: ‘In this paper we formulate and prove several variants of the Erdős-Turán additive bases conjecture.’ The introduction and Section 2 describe the conjecture as ‘remains unresolved’ and ‘a full resolution remains elusive’. Conjecture 7.2 (a stronger version about a count of axes, ν(n,B)) is presented as open. Theorem 4.6 in v3 (as summarised) gives limsup of the axis count = ∞ under density and energy hypotheses.
events.revisions: v2 9 Jun 2021 (no content note read). v3 12 Mar 2026: ‘reformatted and introduction expanded; ideas remain unchanged’ (comments field). arXiv admin note flags overlapping text with arXiv:1803.09155, 1706.09803, 2007.02697.
events.delivers: Variants only: results under extra density or energy hypotheses, and about the axis count ν(n,B) rather than the representation count r(n). Section 4 says it proves ‘some weaker version of the conjecture by imposing some suitable conditions’. It does not claim the original conjecture.
events.remains: The original conjecture for r(n), without the density or energy hypotheses.
events.time_since_posted: about 6 years (v1); about 7 months since v3
events.doubts: The overlap flag from arXiv admins with three other arXiv papers is recorded here as a fact, not a judgement. The v3 Theorem 4.6 proof was not read beyond a search snippet. The conjecture’s statement in Conjecture 7.2 (‘for any 0 < ε ≤ 1/2’) is reported by a summary as problematic as written; I did not verify that.
events.direction: Partial and variant results; they do not cut against the conjecture and do not establish it.

events.what_happened: Theophilus Agama, arXiv:1707.05679, version v4 (18 Jun 2021), retitled ‘An extension of the Erdős-Turán additive base conjecture via generalized circles of partition’. The v4 abstract says: ‘As an application we prove an analogue of the Erdős-Turán additive base conjecture.’ v5 (9 Mar 2022) keeps the ‘analogue’ wording. v1 (16 Jul 2017) and v3 (10 Sep 2018) carry a different title and paper, ‘The master function and applications’, which does not mention the conjecture. v2 (1 Aug 2017) was withdrawn.
events.revisions: v1 16 Jul 2017 (‘The master function and applications’, unrelated); v2 1 Aug 2017 withdrawn; v3 10 Sep 2018 (same unrelated paper); v4 18 Jun 2021 (first version with the Erdős–Turán framing); v5 9 Mar 2022 (‘analogue’); v6 5 Jan 2024 (full claim, next event); v7 13 Feb 2024; v8 8 Mar 2024.
events.delivers: From the abstract only: an analogue of the Erdős–Turán conjecture, via generalized circles of partition. The analogue is not identified in the abstract, and I did not extract it from the body. It is not presented as the conjecture itself.
events.remains: The conjecture itself, which this version describes only as an analogue.
events.doubts: The arXiv identifier carries a different paper in v1 to v3. The scope changed between versions: the Erdős–Turán framing begins only at v4 (2021), and the claim grew from ‘analogue’ (2021, 2022) to ‘prove the conjecture’ (2024).
events.direction: Claimed analogue; the abstract does not say which way the analogue cuts relative to the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Theophilus Agama, arXiv:1707.05679, version v6 (5 Jan 2024), v7 (13 Feb 2024) and v8 (8 Mar 2024, latest). The abstract of v8 says: ‘As an application we prove the Erdős-Turán additive base conjecture.’ Corollary 2.6 is headed ‘Proof of the Erdős-Turán additive base conjecture’ (per the fetch). It concludes that #{(q,r): q+r = n, q,r in A} → ∞ as n → ∞, under (i) a positivity hypothesis on the axis count for all large n, which Remark 2.7 says is the conjecture’s own hypothesis restated, and (ii) |A ∩ ℕ_n| ≥ n^(1−ε) for ε with 0 < ε ≤ 1/2. Remark 2.7 calls Corollary 2.6 ‘a stronger version’ of the conjecture.
events.revisions: v6 5 Jan 2024 is the first version carrying the full claim (its date precedes the 26 Jan 2024 frozen revision). v7 13 Feb 2024 and v8 8 Mar 2024 fall inside the window and keep the claim. No journal reference on the arXiv page. Earlier versions: v4 18 Jun 2021 and v5 9 Mar 2022 claim an analogue only.
events.delivers: As the corollary is stated, for bases satisfying (i) and (ii): a limit (→ ∞) of the ordered-pair count. Restrictions: (1) the conclusion is a limit, stronger than limsup = ∞; (2) condition (ii) at ε = 1/2 is automatic up to a constant for every order-2 asymptotic basis, by the elementary inequality (|A ∩ [0,n]|)^2 ≥ n − C; for smaller ε it is a genuine restriction; the corollary’s quantifier (‘for any 0 < ε ≤ 1/2’ as quoted in Remark 2.7) does not settle which reading applies; (3) condition (i) as stated. The author’s Remark 2.8 says that a ‘trivial proof of the conjecture does not follow from this inequality’.
events.remains: Whether the proof is valid; if it is, the restricted class under (i)–(ii) is covered. What is not covered: whether condition (ii) restricts the class (depends on ε, see delivers); whether the argument extends to all bases; whether limsup = ∞ follows for all bases. Under the bullet’s literal limit form, the corollary’s conclusion matches the wording; under the literature’s limsup form, it is stronger than needed.
events.time_since_posted: 33 months since v6 (5 Jan 2024); 31 months since v8
events.directly_checkable: Corollary 2.6 and the axis-count hypothesis are checkable on a given basis in principle. I did not check them.
events.doubts: (1) Remark 2.8, quoted from the arXiv HTML of v8: ‘The main point is that the first supposed inequality does not always hold for certain subset of the integers’; ‘Nonetheless, it holds for CoPs with natural number base set.’; ‘However, a trivial proof of the conjecture does not follow from this inequality, since the term H(n) could be small in magnitude in a way that dwarfs the contribution from’ (the sentence is cut off in the fetch). The author therefore concedes that the step deducing the conjecture is not established. (2) The author’s own arXiv:2010.11857 v3 (12 Mar 2026) still says the conjecture ‘remains unresolved’ and does not refer to the 2024 claim in any passage I read; I did not check its bibliography for a citation of 1707.05679. (3) Scope and title changed between versions (see agama-2021-analogue). (4) No journal reference, no zbMATH or MathSciNet review, no expert reading, and no refutation was found. (5) Track-record signal, not a verdict on this paper: the author’s 2017 claimed proof of Lemoine’s conjecture (arXiv:1709.05335, with Gensel) carries a v6 comment (21 Mar 2021) saying ‘The first proof of the Little Lemma was wrong and still under construction. So the current proof is conditional and will be completed!!’; v9 (Nov 2023) reframes it as asymptotic results. Wikipedia’s Lemoine article says the 2017 claimed proof was ‘later found to be flawed’.
events.direction: Claims unboundedness of order-2 representation counts (the conjecture’s own direction), but only for the restricted class in the corollary, and the claim is unsupported by the author’s own Remark 2.8.

events.what_happened: A preprint titled ‘A Proof of the Erdos-Turan Conjecture on Asymptotic Additive Bases’ is listed at osf.io/preprints/osf/mxgbu_v1, dated June 2024 by a search summary. The OSF page returned only the text ‘OSF’ to both fetch attempts, so the author, abstract, date and argument are unverified.
events.delivers: Unknown. By its title, a full proof of the conjecture for asymptotic bases of order 2. Not verified.
events.time_since_posted: about 28 months if the date is right
events.doubts: Unread. Authorship is unknown, so I cannot say whether it is independent of the Agama claim. The title claims the same result as Agama’s 2024 version.
events.direction: Claims unboundedness (by title only).

events.what_happened: Yuchen Ding and Lilu Zhao, ‘A new upper bound on Ruzsa’s number on the Erdős–Turán conjecture’, arXiv:2307.12311 (v1 23 Jul 2023; v6 27 Aug 2023). The Ruzsa number R_m is at most 192 for every positive integer m, improving Chen’s 288. Published in Int. J. Number Theory 20 (2024), 1515–1523 (online 6 Apr 2024, per a search summary; not opened).
events.revisions: v1 23 Jul 2023 to v6 27 Aug 2023. Journal version online 6 Apr 2024 (per search summary); the journal date is not the first-argument date.
events.delivers: An upper bound R_m ≤ 192 for Ruzsa numbers in Z_m. The result is modular, so it says nothing about the integers.

checked_by.who: International Journal of Number Theory (World Scientific)
checked_by.what_they_did: published the paper (online 6 Apr 2024, per search summary)

checked_by.who: Yong-Gao Chen (named in the arXiv comments field)
checked_by.qualification: the author of the prior bound 288 and an expert in this area
checked_by.what_they_did: pointed out gaps, which the authors say they corrected (per the comments field)

events.direction: Upper bound on a modular quantity; neighbouring; no direction on the integer conjecture.

events.what_happened: Guangping Liang, Yu Zhang and Haode Zuo, ‘Additive and subtractive bases of Z_m in average’, arXiv:2407.02344 (July 2024 per the identifier), published in the Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society. They prove limsup of the average-version quantity ℓ_m ≤ 144 over Z_m. A correction note (Feb 2025, per search summary) says a bound |A_1| ≤ 2|B| should read |A_1| ≤ |B| (credited to Honghu Liu).
events.revisions: arXiv v2 exists (listing). Bull. Aust. Math. Soc. correction, Feb 2025 (per search summary).
events.delivers: A modular average-version bound (≤ 144) over Z_m. Not the integer problem.
events.doubts: The correction note changes a constant in the argument (per summary). I did not open the paper or the correction.
events.direction: Modular upper bound; neighbouring; no direction on the integer conjecture.

events.what_happened: Daniel Larsen and Michael Larsen, ‘Robust additive bases without minimal subbases’, arXiv:2601.18507 (single version, 26 Jan 2026). They construct a set A of positive integers with r_A(m) > ε log m for all large m that contains no minimal additive subbasis of order 2. erdosproblems.com credits this as ‘answered in the negative by Larsen and Larsen’ for the second part of Problem 868 (the ‘ε log n’ question). It does not address the Erdős–Turán conjecture.
events.delivers: A logarithmic lower bound r_A(m) > ε log m with any ε > 0 does not force a minimal subbasis. The question is about minimal subbases. The construction has r_A → ∞, so it is consistent with the conjecture, but it does not show that every order-2 basis has unbounded counts.
events.doubts: The erdosproblems.com page for Problem 868 cites a PDF on the authors’ GitHub. A forum commenter says a unified preprint should be written. A forum post on Problem 870 says the Larsen–Larsen preprint is ‘not straightforwardly formalizable’ (search summary).
events.direction: Negative answer to a neighbouring question. No direction on the conjecture, and the object is compatible with it.
events.object: A set A with r_A(m) > ε log m for all sufficiently large m and no D ⊂ A that is a minimal asymptotic basis of order 2. The method was not read from the paper; a forum comment (via search summary) calls it a probabilistic random construction, which I did not verify.

events.what_happened: Daniel Larsen, ‘Three Questions of Erdős–Nathanson on Asymptotic Bases of Order 2’, arXiv:2603.03472 (v1 3 Mar 2026, 7 pages, math.NT). For slower growth rates than the Erdős–Nathanson logarithmic threshold, the three properties (divergent representation function; decomposability into two bases; containing a minimal basis) are shown to be independent. Introduction reports the author’s earlier negative answer to Erdős–Nathanson Question 2 (the 871 result) via a multiagent system.
events.delivers: Independence of three robustness properties of order-2 asymptotic bases under weaker growth rates. It does not address whether the representation count must be unbounded for all bases.
events.remains: The Erdős–Turán conjecture entirely. The paper says nothing on it.
events.doubts: The abstract-page fetch reported no AI mention. The full HTML does contain AI sentences (listed below). I rely on the HTML.
events.direction: Independence results; no direction on the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Erdős Problem 871 is recorded on erdosproblems.com as ‘Disproved’ (Lean-verified). The question: if 1_A*1_A(n) → ∞, can A be partitioned into two disjoint additive bases of order 2? The site says: ‘This has been disproved by Larsen using Claude Opus 4.5, in fact only a small modification of the argument of [ErNa89] is required.’ The erdosproblems AI-contributions wiki dates it 5 Jan 2026 with ‘Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro’ and status ‘Existing partial result upgraded to full solution (Lean)’. The author’s arXiv paper 2603.03472 describes the same result (its Question 2) as shown ‘by the author, using a multiagent system built on Claude 4.5 and Gemini 3 Pro’. No arXiv write-up of this disproof was found.
events.revisions: The site’s history page was not opened; the date comes from the AI-contributions wiki. A forum thread (871) exists and was not read in full.
events.delivers: A basis A of order 2 with 1_A*1_A(n) → ∞ that is not a union of two disjoint asymptotic bases of order 2. The hypothesis is divergence of r, the conjecture’s conclusion in its strong (limit) form, so the result is a counterexample to the Erdős–Nathanson question and does not decide whether r must diverge.
events.remains: The Erdős–Turán conjecture entirely, since the result takes divergence as a hypothesis.

checked_by.who: Lean formalisation (the site’s label ‘DISPROVED (LEAN)’); an unnamed forum commenter who says the Lean proof follows the Erdős–Nathanson method closely
checked_by.what_they_did: formalised the disproof in Lean; commenter compared the argument with Erdős–Nathanson

events.doubts: The AI credit differs across sources: the site says ‘Claude Opus 4.5’; the wiki says ‘Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro’; the author’s paper says ‘a multiagent system built on Claude 4.5 and Gemini 3 Pro’. The site’s thanks to Tao, van Doorn and Larsen are acknowledgements, not endorsements. A forum comment says the same method ‘should resolve’ the first half of Problem 868, attributed on the site to Claude Opus 4.5.
events.direction: Negative answer to the Erdős–Nathanson question; neighbouring. No direction on the Erdős–Turán conjecture.
events.object: A basis A of order 2 with divergent representation function that cannot be partitioned into two disjoint order-2 bases. Per a forum comment (via search summary), the construction adapts the Erdős–Nathanson 1989 argument and lets a parameter F_k grow very slowly. Explicit or non-constructive status not read.

systems.name: Claude Opus 4.5
systems.what_it_did: Per erdosproblems.com, the disproof was done ‘by Larsen using Claude Opus 4.5’. The site’s wording does not say what the model produced beyond that.

systems.basis_quote: This was previously shown not to be the case by the author, using a multiagent system built on Claude 4.5 and Gemini 3 Pro, with a construction based on [2].

systems.name: Gemini 3 Pro
systems.what_it_did: Part of the multiagent system the author describes for the earlier disproof of Question 2 (see the Claude 4.5 entry).
systems.basis_quote: This was previously shown not to be the case by the author, using a multiagent system built on Claude 4.5 and Gemini 3 Pro, with a construction based on [2].

events.what_happened: David Turturean, a Lean 4 formalisation and a natural-language negative answer to Erdős Problem 870, repository ‘Erdos870’ (‘Additive bases with many representations and no minimal subbasis’). Problem 870 (per the erdosproblems page) concerns order k ≥ 3: whether a logarithmic lower bound on representations as a sum of at most k elements forces a minimal basis of order k. The repository says ‘no constant c(k) can force a minimal subbasis from a logarithmic representation lower bound’, and builds on the Larsen–Larsen order-two construction. The AI wiki dates the natural-language work to 24 Apr–2 May 2026 with status ‘Candidate full solution’. The Lean repository was last updated 8 Aug 2026.
events.revisions: Lean repository last updated 8 Aug 2026 (commit a732dee per the page). Work period 24 Apr–2 May 2026 per the AI wiki; the first public posting date is not established.
events.delivers: For order k ≥ 3, no constant c(k) forces a minimal subbasis from a logarithmic lower bound on representations (per the repository description). Restricted to the order-k variant; it does not address the order-2 unboundedness question.
events.doubts: The sorry-free status is the author’s own claim on the Lean reservoir page, and I did not check the code. The AI wiki lists the status as ‘Candidate full solution’, not as a full solution. Forum threads on Problem 870 were not read.
events.direction: Negative answer for the order-k variant. Neighbouring; no direction on the Erdős–Turán conjecture.

events.what_happened: Boris Alexeev, Moe Putterman, Mehtaab Sawhney, Mark Sellke and Gregory Valiant, ‘Short proofs in combinatorics and number theory’, arXiv:2603.29961 (31 Mar 2026; v2 2 Apr 2026). Three short proofs, each answering a question raised by Erdős. The second concerns whether an additive basis A can be split into A_1 and A_2, each with A_i + A_i of bounded gaps. The abstract says: ‘In each case, the proof is due entirely to an internal model at OpenAI.’
events.delivers: A splitting result about A_i + A_i with bounded gaps (per abstract). Not about representation counts; no bearing on unboundedness.
events.doubts: Only the abstract was read, so the exact statement of the splitting question is unverified. The AI wiki and a search summary tie a similar splitting question to Erdős 1051 (Aletheia, Jan–Feb 2026); I did not verify that link.
events.direction: A positive answer to a splitting question, as summarised. Neighbouring; no direction on the conjecture.

systems.name: an internal model at OpenAI
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors’ abstract, produced the proofs of the three problems, including the additive-basis splitting proof.

events.what_happened: Yuchen Ding, Yu-Chen Sun and Lilu Zhao, ‘An improved upper bound on the Ruzsa number’, arXiv:2607.06167 (v1 7 Jul 2026). They prove R_m ≤ 128 for every positive integer m, improving 192 (per the abstract).
events.delivers: A modular bound R_m ≤ 128. It concerns Z_m, not the integers.
events.doubts: Not peer reviewed as of posting.
events.direction: Modular upper bound; neighbouring; no direction on the integer conjecture.

disputes.summary: Two 2024 proof claims: Agama’s arXiv:1707.05679 v6–v8 (Jan–Mar 2024) and an OSF preprint with the same title (June 2024, per a search summary, unread). Whether they are independent is unknown.

The same author’s arXiv:2010.11857 v3 (12 Mar 2026) says the conjecture ‘remains unresolved’, while arXiv:1707.05679 v8 (8 Mar 2024) says ‘we prove the Erdős-Turán additive base conjecture’. No reconciliation was found.

AI credit for Erdős 871 differs by source: erdosproblems.com ‘Claude Opus 4.5’; AI wiki ‘Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro’ (5 Jan 2026); author’s 2603.03472 ‘a multiagent system built on Claude 4.5 and Gemini 3 Pro’. For Erdős 868, erdosproblems credits ‘Larsen and Larsen’, while the AI wiki lists ‘GPT-5.2 multi-agent system’ (13 Jan 2026, partial result). The arXiv paper 2601.18507 (26 Jan 2026) contains no AI mention, and the Larsen–Larsen paper is single-version.

The 1956 result: the Waterloo MSc thesis (Xiao 2011) says Erdős gave ‘a positive answer’ for h = 2 in 1956. The Wikipedia article and later summaries describe the 1956 result as the existence of order-2 bases with r(n) = O(log n), an upper bound that does not decide unboundedness. Recorded as a dispute, not resolved.

Lower bounds on limsup r(n) conflict across sources: Grekos–Haddad–Helou–Pihko 6 (5 in one summary); Borwein–Choi–Chu 7 (‘cannot be bounded by 7’, so ≥ 8 in later summaries). Also, Tang–Chen’s modular bound is 768 in one summary and 5120 in another.

The bullet asks that the count ‘tend to infinity’ (a limit). Erdős–Turán 1941 (as summarised by Wikipedia), Nathanson and Agama’s Conjecture 1.1 state limsup = ∞. Agama’s Corollary 2.6 concludes a limit, which matches the bullet’s wording but is stronger than the literature statement.
arXiv:1707.05679 carries an unrelated paper (‘The master function and applications’) in v1 to v3 (2017–2018). The Erdős–Turán framing appears only from v4 (2021).

summary: Every standard reference I opened still lists the conjecture as open: the Wikipedia article (lead: ‘an old unsolved problem’), the Open Problem Garden entry (importance 4 of 4 and a $500 Erdős–Graham prize, which I did not check against the prize terms), the erdosproblems.com neighbours, and Agama’s own March 2026 paper. I found no refereed or expert engagement with any claimed proof, and no AI system credited with the conjecture itself. The only claim of a full proof falling inside the window is Theophilus Agama’s arXiv:1707.05679. Its v6 (5 Jan 2024, before the frozen revision) first carries ‘As an application we prove the Erdős-Turán additive base conjecture’, and v7 (13 Feb 2024) and v8 (8 Mar 2024) keep it. The arXiv text (v8 HTML) gives Corollary 2.6, which concludes a limit under two hypotheses. Hypothesis (ii) at ε = 1/2 holds for every asymptotic order-2 basis up to a constant, so whether the corollary is restricted depends on which ε the corollary uses; that is a close call for the later pass. Remark 2.8 concedes that ‘a trivial proof of the conjecture does not follow from this inequality’ because H(n) may be small. The version history shows the paper was a different one until v4 (2021), with an ‘analogue’ claim in 2021–2022 and the full claim first in January 2024. A track-record note: the author’s 2017 Lemoine-conjecture proof was reported by its own comment (21 Mar 2021) as having a wrong key lemma, and was reframed as asymptotic results in November 2023. The OSF preprint with the same title as a proof (June 2024, per a search summary) could not be read. Neighbouring events, all of which bear on Erdős–Nathanson or splitting questions rather than unboundedness, are recorded separately: the Larsen–Larsen minimal-subbasis counterexample (Jan 2026, no AI mention), the Erdős 871 disproof (Jan 2026, with AI credited by the site and by the author), the Larsen 2026 independence paper (Mar 2026; its HTML credits Claude Sonnet 4.5 with graphics and ChatGPT 5.2 Pro with proofreading), the Turturean order-k negative answer for Problem 870 (Apr–May 2026, AI-heavy, Lean repository), and the OpenAI short-proofs preprint (31 Mar 2026) on an additive-basis splitting question, credited to ‘an internal model at OpenAI’. Pre-2024 partial results (Dirac 1951; Erdős 1956 and Erdős–Tetali 1990 on economical bases; Borwein–Choi–Chu 2005/2006, limsup ≥ 8; Sándor 2008; Grekos–Haddad–Helou–Pihko, year uncertain; Konstantoulas 2013) are lower bounds or upper bounds that do not settle the conjecture. Modular results (Tang–Chen 2008 counterexample in Z_m; Ding–Zhao 2023 and Ding–Sun–Zhao 2026 Ruzsa-number bounds; Liang–Zhang–Zuo 2024) cut against a naive modular analogue but say nothing about the integers. The Quanta piece on AI and Erdős problems (3 Aug 2026, read only as excerpts) and the OpenAI Astra list (1 Aug 2026, read through coverage) do not name this problem.
competing_reading: The strongest case for counting the Agama 2024 claim as a resolution of the bullet: the bullet asks for a limit, Corollary 2.6 concludes a limit, the ε = 1/2 density hypothesis is automatic for every asymptotic order-2 basis (up to a constant), so the corollary may cover all bases; and the claim appeared in January 2024, before the frozen revision, and was kept in the window. Against: the author’s own Remark 2.8 concedes that the step deducing the conjecture is not established; the paper has no referee record; its scope changed between versions; and the same author’s March 2026 paper calls the conjecture unresolved. The case for ‘nothing happened’ is the stronger reading on present evidence. A second reading exists for the Xiao thesis: its ‘positive answer … in 1956’ could be read as a claimed earlier resolution, but the 1956 result as described elsewhere is an upper-bound existence theorem, so I treat it as a misstatement.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A referee report, journal acceptance or expert write-up of arXiv:1707.05679 v8, and in particular the step Remark 2.8 says is not trivial; (2) the text of the OSF preprint ‘A Proof of the Erdos-Turan Conjecture on Asymptotic Additive Bases’ (author, date, argument); (3) the value of ε used in Corollary 2.6 and whether condition (ii) excludes any basis; (4) whether arXiv:2010.11857 v3 or any later paper cites 1707.05679 and what it says; (5) an erdosproblems.com or Bloom entry for the conjecture itself, if one exists (none located); (6) the original Borwein–Choi–Chu 2006 paper, to fix the lower bound constant; (7) the Larsen–Larsen construction method and the Erdős 871 forum thread, to fix the AI attribution.

incomplete: (1) The OSF preprint (June 2024, ‘A Proof of the Erdos-Turan Conjecture on Asymptotic Additive Bases’) could not be read: both the short link and the preprint URL returned only the word ‘OSF’. Its authorship, date, and argument are unverified, and it is recorded as an unread lead. (2) The OpenAI preprint catalogue (Pitt mirror, which search summaries describe as listing 722 OpenAI manuscripts) exceeded the fetch size limit and was not read. The OpenAI GitHub repository was not searched directly for the conjecture, so the AI search covers the erdosproblems AI wiki, search results, and news coverage, but not the full OpenAI catalogue. (3) Quotes from arXiv full texts were obtained through a summarising fetch tool. Quotes presented as verbatim are the tool’s quotations, and some are cut off. Load-bearing quotes (Agama Corollary 2.6 and Remarks 2.7–2.8; the Larsen 2603.03472 AI sentences; the Turturean quotation on the Lean repository page; the OpenAI abstract sentence) should be checked against the source before reliance. The PDF of arXiv:1707.05679 v8 was binary and unreadable, so the HTML was used. (4) The Agama v7 version was not opened separately; its claim is inferred from the listing and the v8 text. (5) The following were read only from search summaries and not opened: Grekos–Haddad–Helou–Pihko (year uncertain; the 6 vs 5 value conflicts), Sándor 2008, Konstantoulas 2013, Tang–Chen 2008 (constant conflicts: 768 vs 5120), Ruzsa 1990, Ding–Zhao’s journal publication, the Liang–Zhang–Zuo paper and its 2025 correction, and the Erdős 871 and 868 forum threads and history pages (the 871 date is from the AI wiki). (6) zbMATH and MathSciNet were not checked. (7) The Wikipedia article was read as it stands now, not as it stood on 26 January 2024. (8) No Lean or Mathlib formalisation of the conjecture was located, so the sorry status for it is unknown. (9) The Erdős–Turán conjecture has no erdosproblems.com entry that I could find, so the site’s status for this conjecture is unknown. (10) The Agama 2010.11857 v3 bibliography was not checked for a citation of arXiv:1707.05679.
